findings.function: every role-gated function (Strings.toHexString inlined in AccessControl._checkRole), e.g. pause()
findings.lines: e.g. pause: 'while idx > 1: if idx >= 42: revert with Panic(50)' and 'if idx >= 66: revert with Panic(50)' (44 instances)
findings.decompiled: idx = 41 / s = caller / while idx > 1: / if idx >= 42: revert with Panic(50) / mem[idx + 160 len 1] = byte(s % 16, 0x3031...6566...) / idx = idx - 1 / s = s / 16
findings.source: Strings.sol:64-67 for (uint256 i = 2 * length + 1; i > 1; --i) { buffer[i] = _SYMBOLS[value & 0xf]; value >>= 4; }
findings.issue: The bounds check of buffer[i] is kept in every iteration although i starts at 2 * length + 1 = 41 (or 65), below the buffer length 42 (66), and only decreases.
findings.rule: For a loop variable with initial value a and only decreasing steps (guarded by i > 1, so no wrap), i <= a holds in the body; a check i >= n with a < n is dead and can be dropped.

notes: Small, clean text. The only source loop is OZ Strings.toHexString, inlined twice in each role-gated function (address and role); its 'while idx > 1' is exact, and the whole AccessControl revert is decoded into one 'revert with Error(string reason), 32, 148, ..., mem[162 len 40], ' is missing role 0x', mem[258 len 64]' line with the '0x' prefix folded into the literal. Reviewed in detail: pause / unpause, onStEthAllocated (reentrancy, pause, role, timelocked pending order, balance checks), getters and role management; the other setters are the same pattern. P8 counts the hash-scratch writes kept before hasRole[...][caller] reads; P11 the dead buffer bounds checks of the finding.
summary: Faithful and readable: the single source loop is a clean while and the AccessControl message is fully decoded; only dead bounds checks, hash scratch writes and zero immutables remain.
